newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity futures end higher, PV steady.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity futures end higher, PV steady.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures closed Thursday with Palo Verde (PV) contracts steady and California-Oregon Border (COB) contracts higher in a move that traders and brokers found difficult to explain.
"There seems to be more interest over the last couple of days, but the up movement was a mystery," said one futures broker.
"(Physical electricity) day prices are a little higher, which probably had some effect," said another broker.
October COB settled 45 cents higher at $16.55 after trade in a range of $16.20-16.75, while November COB closed up 35 cents at $17.15 from trade in a range of $16.85-16.90 per megawatt hour (MWh).
Remaining COB deferreds finished between five and 20 cents higher.
October PV ended four cents higher at $16.84 after trade in a range of $16.55-16.90 per MWh, while most remaining PV deferreds held steady without trading.
NYMEX said an estimated total of 339 COB and 164 PV contracts traded.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
